title: Health Trends 2027
summary: Employer health trends 2027: high medical costs, AI impacts and value-focused strategies for employers.
body_markdown:
## Top findings from our survey


###


High healthcare costs are now structural, not temporary. The trend hits 10.1% in 2027 — the seventh straight double-digit year. Employers should plan for sustained pressure, not a one-off renewal spike.


###


AI cuts both ways. Most insurers (55%) expect it to lower costs through automation and fraud detection — but it can also raise them via new tech spend and higher utilization. AI isn't an automatic win; it requires employer oversight.


###


Cutting coverage alone isn't sustainable. A third of insurers expect employers to shift toward optimizing value instead — spending smarter, not just less. There's no single fix; the right lever mix depends on each workforce.


###


Cancer is still the top cost driver (70% of insurers), and advanced treatments are raising the stakes. Yet fewer than half of plans cover key screenings. Employers should support the full journey — prevention through survivorship — not just treatment.
